findings.rationale: ComposeItem::Internal with an unknown alias is a silent no-op, leaving the intended action public. The hiding set is built at line 291-298 from ComposeItem::Internal { alias, action } and matched at line 326 only to suppress a component action when `(alias, name)` is present. There is no check that `alias` names an actually `Use`d component (the Use loop at line 263-290 validates Use aliases but not Internal aliases) or that `action` is a real action of that component. Consequently an Internal item with a typo'd or non-existent alias never matches and is silently ignored, so the action the author intended to keep internal remains exposed in the composed kernel. The documented contract (line 253-254) promises CoreError for unknown aliases, but this path raises no error — a silent misconfiguration. Whether parse-level validation already rejects such Internal items is not visible in this projection.

Lvalue rewrite ignores the `bound` set, so a binder that shadows a component state name silently writes to global state. rewrite_expr (line 709-717) prefixes Expr::Var only when the name is NOT in `bound`, so binder variables stay local on the RHS. But rewrite_lvalue (line 687-698) routes LValue::Var/LValue::Index through rewrite_state_name (line 700-706), which prefixes the name whenever it matches component.names.state with NO `bound` check. Trigger: a component exposes state `x`, and a composed statement contains `forAll (x : <range>) { x := <rhs using x> }` where the ForAll binder `x` shadows state `x`. rewrite_statement (line 670-683) correctly adds the binder name to `nested` and passes it to the body, so the RHS `x` is left un-prefixed, while the LHS `x` is rewritten to `{alias}.x`. The lowered assignment is `{alias}.x := x`: the binder-local value is written into the component's global state instead of the local binder variable — a silent cross-scope write / data corruption rather than the intended local self-assignment. The same inconsistency applies to LValue::Index, whose name is prefixed while its index expression respects `bound`.
